title: Indium Tin Oxide Substrates Enable Coating-Free SEM Imaging and Simplified Preparation of Purified Fibrinogen Clots
content:
Abstract
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of fibrin fibers typically requires time-consuming preparation and conductive sputter coating, which can alter nanoscale structural measurements. Additionally, protocols for purified fibrinogen clots often include unnecessary steps adapted from plasma clot methods. We aimed to evaluate indium tin oxide (ITO) as a flat, conductive SEM substrate, investigate sputter coating effects on fiber diameter, and simplify purified fibrinogen clot preparation. Platelet-poor plasma and purified fibrinogen clots were formed on ITO substrates and imaged via SEM after 0, 45, or 90 s of sputter coating to quantify diameter variations. For purified clots, a simplified protocol—forming and imaging clots directly on ITO—was compared against a standardized workflow involving clot transfer from microtube lids to carbon tape. Sputter coating duration significantly affected fiber measurements, with longer coating times increasing apparent diameters. Plasma and purified clots showed distinct responses. Crucially, the simplified ITO protocol produced fiber diameter measurements that did not differ significantly from the standardized workflow under identical coating conditions. ITO is an effective conductive substrate that simplifies purified fibrinogen clot preparation by eliminating washing and transfer steps. It yields comparable diameter measurements to standard methods, offering an efficient platform for analyzing fibrin structures.
